observations: Photos 0, 1 and 2: the same automatic gearbox (front wheel drive transaxle) with its torque converter fitted, seen from the bell housing side, sitting in a spare parts market among used engines on shelves.
Aluminium case dirty with dust and oil grime; no crack is visible at this resolution.
Oil cooler lines with a rubber hose on top; the hose print reads like a generic SAE hose standard, which does not identify the vehicle.
A white label on the bell housing (photos 0 and 1) and a barcode label on the torque converter (photos 0 and 2) are not legible, so no part number, transmission code or vehicle fitment can be read.
No Ford logo or casting mark is readable in any photo.
Orange paint mark on a torque converter bolt, photos 1 and 2.
Axle output opening and seal visible on the lower left of the case; the transmission control plug and valve body side are not shown.
Watermark 'GEARUP INC' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' on every photo, so these are a parts dealer's photos.
The seller asks for the buyer's engine capacity, which suggests a stock advert for several units rather than one fixed gearbox.

identity.kind: used automatic gearbox, front wheel drive transaxle with torque converter (vehicle fitment not readable)
read_from: photos 0, 1 and 2 overall shape: transaxle case with torque converter and cooler lines

claims.evidence: Photos 0 to 2 show an automatic transaxle with torque converter.
No Ford logo, tag or part number is legible; the bell housing label and converter barcode cannot be read.
Origin cannot be shown in photos.
The transmission code that would tie it to a 4 cylinder engine is not legible.

claims.claim: Available, tell us your engine capacity
claims.evidence: Implies more than one unit; nothing shows which gearbox would actually be supplied.

risks.risk: The gearbox may not be a Ford Fusion 4 cylinder unit; fitment and transmission code set the price and are unreadable.
risks.proof: A sharp close up of the identification label on the bell housing showing the part number and transmission code.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot be priced as a Ford Fusion gearbox; no price until fitment is read.

risks.risk: Internal wear: slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, worn clutches or a failing torque converter.
risks.proof: A clip of the gearbox running in a car, or a test on the dealer's bench, shifting through all gears.
Photo of fluid drained or on the dipstick against white paper.

risks.risk: Solenoid, valve body or electrical connector damaged or missing.
risks.proof: Photos of the valve body side and the electrical connector.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as needing valve body and solenoid repair.

risks.risk: Cracked case or broken mounting lugs hidden by grime or the angle.
risks.proof: Photos of all sides of the case after a wipe down, including mounts.

risks.risk: The unit supplied may differ from the one photographed.
risks.proof: A photo of the exact unit with a handwritten note bearing today's date and a code we supply, next to its label.
risks.if_unproven: Quote conditional on the agent matching the label before payment.

proof_requests: A sharp close up of the identification label on the bell housing with part number and transmission code.
The same unit beside a handwritten note with today's date and our code.
A clip of the gearbox tested, shifting through all gears.
Photos of the valve body side, electrical connector and mounts.
Photo of the fluid against white paper.
response.reason: The photos show an automatic front wheel drive transaxle, but nothing readable ties it to a Ford Fusion or a 4 cylinder engine, and a gearbox is priced by its fitment code. One close up of the bell housing label settles the identity, after which it can be priced as needing rebuild until a test clip is sent.
